sentences.text: Aegirosaurus is an extinct genus of ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaurs belonging to the subfamily Platypterygiinae.
The neotype specimen measures 1.77 meters in length, while the destroyed holotype was estimated to be about 2 meters long.
The eye sockets contain a scleral ring made of 14 bony plates that occupies most of the space within the orbit.
Aegirosaurus possessed a tail fin shaped like a crescent moon.
Skin impressions on the neotype revealed wavy textures, straight fibrous tissue, and structures resembling very small scales.
The species was originally described by Wagner in 1853 as Ichthyosaurus leptospondylus.
Bardet and Fernández selected a neotype specimen in 2000 after the original holotype was destroyed in World War II.
The genus name Aegirosaurus translates to 'Aegir lizard with slender vertebrae', referring to the Norse sea god Aegir.
Fossils of Aegirosaurus have been found in the Lower Tithonian (Upper Jurassic) of Bavaria, Germany.
Aegirosaurus remains have also been discovered in the late Valanginian (early Cretaceous) of southeastern France.
The presence of Aegirosaurus in both periods suggests that many late Jurassic ichthyosaurs survived across the Jurassic-Cretaceous boundary.
Aegirosaurus lived from 149.2 to 132.6 million years ago, spanning the Tithonian to Valanginian periods.
